title: Model file, schema version 32
description: A discrete-event model: blocks, the links between them, the resources they seize, and the run settings. Generated from the live registries (nagasim.modelschema). RECORD kinds: count, tally, time_between, time_persistent, cost. CREATE arrival modes: Interarrival, Schedule, Orders.

$schema.description: This schema's URL, for an editor's completion and checks; the engine ignores it.

schema_version.description: Older files migrate on load; a newer one is refused.

background.description: Optional floor-plan image behind the canvas; ignored by the engine.

description.description: A short description of the model.

written_by.description: The nagasim version that last saved the file, written on every save (D1193).

labels.description: Which blocks the editor labels: all, only assets, or none.

node_names.description: Whether the editor shows network node names on hover or always.

outputs.description: OPTIONAL extra output collection whose cost is opt-in . Absent, none of it runs.

bottleneck.description: Collect per-resource ACTIVE intervals for the Roser bottleneck analyser ("bottleneck_summary"). Off by default: the intervals cost memory proportional to the event count.

schedule.description: Record one row per resource hold ("schedule_log") for the schedule Gantt and the plan export. Off by default; forced on in deterministic mode ("simulation.deterministic").

view.description: Editor view state, written by the editor on save; ignored by the engine. Absent keys are the defaults: Process tab, schematic, every tab fitted to its contents.

tab.description: The editor tab in front when the file was saved.

layout.description: Whether the editor was in layout mode.

queue_display.description: How the 3D view stacks waiting items: compact (per-form limits, the default) or tall (layers without limit).

draw_guard.description: The 3D view pauses playback before drawing more than limit items (default 20000); the 2D canvas skips a frame's new moves past limit_2d tokens (default 50000). On by default.

layers.description: Which 3D layers show: a kind (equipment, tiles, names, pads, items, floor, building, network) or a block's user layer, to true or false; missing is shown.

canvases.description: The zoom and centre of each canvas tab.

exits.description: One name per exit, in exit order; "name:target" names the CONVEYOR a part counts as under way to. Empty: the exits' own names.

conditions.description: For "condition": one expression per exit, or one fewer (the last exit is the ELSE).

limit.description: Parts under way to one exit at most; 0: no limit.

attribute.description: For "attribute": the entity attribute whose value names the exit.

structural_argument.description: Inside a submodel definition only: bind this param to the instance's argument of that name. Flattening replaces it with the argument's value, coerced to the param's declared type, so the engine never sees one.

dist_params.description: Parameters of the sibling `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). Each value is a number or an expression string. See $defs/duration for the per-distribution parameter lists.

duration.description: A duration spec: a distribution, its parameters and an optional unit. Used by link delays and failure uptime/downtime.

oneOf.title: Bernoulli
oneOf.description: A single yes/no outcome with a given probability, such as accept or reject, pass or fail, or rework or not. Param: p (success probability) in [0, 1].

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Beta
oneOf.description: A value between a minimum and a maximum with a flexible shape, such as a fraction, a proportion or a bounded time. Params: alpha, beta > 0; min < max.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Binomial
oneOf.description: Count of successes (for example defective parts) in a fixed number of independent trials. Params: n (trials) >= 0, p in [0, 1].

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: BoundedNormal
oneOf.description: Bell-shaped variation around an average, cut off at a minimum and a maximum so a time cannot go negative or beyond a physical limit. Params: mean (central value), stddev (standard deviation) > 0; min < max.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Cauchy
oneOf.description: Very heavy-tailed values with frequent extreme outliers in both directions; rarely right for times, and it often returns negative values. Params: x0 (location), gamma (scale) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: ChiSquare
oneOf.description: Statistical diagnostics and sums of squared normal variations; rarely used for simulation times. Param: df (degrees of freedom) >= 1.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Constant
oneOf.description: A fixed duration that never varies, for a deterministic service time, transit time or interval. Params: value (fixed duration) >= 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: CustomExpression
oneOf.description: Any model expression, for example '2 + EXPO(3)', when no single distribution fits. Param: expression (string, e.g. '2 + EXPO(3)').

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: DiscreteUniform
oneOf.description: A whole number between a minimum and a maximum, each equally likely, such as a random lot size from 1 to 6. Params: low (min) <= high (max), integers.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: EmpiricalContinuous
oneOf.description: Measured data as a histogram: a bin is picked by its weight, then a value is drawn evenly within it (a continuous draw, not a resample of points). Params: values (float list of bin edges, length = len(probs) + 1), probs (bin weights summing to 1).

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: EmpiricalDiscrete
oneOf.description: Whole-number values with their own measured probabilities, such as order sizes or the number of items per job. Params: values (int list), probs (weights summing to 1).

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Erlang
oneOf.description: Time to finish k exponential steps in a row, giving a service time less variable than exponential but still random. Params: k (stages) >= 1, rate (lambda) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Exponential
oneOf.description: Time between random independent arrivals, or time to a random breakdown, when past events do not change the next one. Param: rate (lambda, event rate) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: FixedSchedule
oneOf.description: Exact listed times, for arrivals or events that follow a fixed timetable such as a roster or a delivery plan; an optional jitter shifts each arrival at random and keeps their order. Params: schedule (ordered list of times), jitter (standard deviation, 0 = off), jitter_law (Normal or Uniform).

schedule.description: ordered list of absolute arrival/event times

jitter.description: standard deviation of each arrival's random shift, in the schedule's unit; 0 = exact times

jitter_law.description: shape of the shift: Normal or Uniform (same standard deviation)

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Gamma
oneOf.description: Right-skewed service or processing times that cannot go below zero, from very regular to very variable. Params: alpha (shape) > 0, beta (scale) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Geometric
oneOf.description: Number of attempts until the first success, such as tries before a part passes inspection. Param: p in (0, 1].

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Hypergeometric
oneOf.description: Successes in a sample drawn without replacement from a finite lot, such as defectives found when inspecting a sample. Params: N (population) >= K (success states) >= n (sample) >= 0.

K.description: number of success states in the population

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: InverseGaussian
oneOf.description: Right-skewed positive times such as a reaction or decision delay, or the time for a drifting quantity to reach a level. Params: mu (mean) > 0, lambda (shape) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: JohnsonSB
oneOf.description: A skewed value that stays between a minimum and a maximum, such as a yield or fill percentage. Params: a1, a2 (shape), min < max.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: JohnsonSU
oneOf.description: A flexible fit for skewed, heavy-tailed data when no simple distribution matches; it can return negative values. Params: a, b (shape), loc (center), scale > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: LogLogistic
oneOf.description: Right-skewed durations with a heavier tail than lognormal, such as repair or lifetime data that cannot go below zero. Params: c (shape) > 0, scale > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Lognormal
oneOf.description: Right-skewed times that cannot go below zero, such as manual handling, picking or repair durations with an occasional long one. Params: mu (log-mean), sigma (log-stddev) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: NegativeBinomial
oneOf.description: Number of failures before a set number of successes, each try with the same chance of success, such as rejected parts before r good ones. Params: r (target successes) >= 1, p in (0, 1].

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Normal
oneOf.description: Symmetric variation around an average, such as a cycle time that is rarely far from the mean; it can go negative unless the mean is much larger than the spread. Params: mean (central value), stddev (standard deviation) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: PearsonTypeV
oneOf.description: Right-skewed positive delays or times to failure with a long tail, an alternative to lognormal. Params: a (shape) > 0, scale > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: PearsonTypeVI
oneOf.description: A ratio of two gamma variables, such as cost per service, that is always positive; it can model times when the parameters suit. Params: a, b > 0, scale > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Poisson
oneOf.description: Counts per period, such as the number of arrivals or events in a fixed time window. Param: lambda (average rate) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Rayleigh
oneOf.description: A positive magnitude such as movement noise or a positioning error, with a single scale parameter. Param: sigma (scale) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Triangular
oneOf.description: Min, most likely and max are known, usually from expert estimates when there is no data. Params: low =< mode =< high.

mode.description: most likely value, between low and high

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Uniform
oneOf.description: Any value between a minimum and a maximum is equally likely; use it when only the min and max are known. Params: low (min) =< high (max), both real numbers.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: Weibull
oneOf.description: Equipment lifetimes and time to failure, where the breakdown rate can rise with age (wear-out) or fall (early failures). Params: scale (lambda) > 0, shape (k) > 0.

time_unit.description: Unit the sampled duration is expressed in.

oneOf.title: ASSIGN
oneOf.description: Sets attributes on a part, order or customer, or a model variable, from expressions as it passes, for example a due date, a type or a counter. Takes an ordered list of assignments, each is `{"target": "entity.<attr>" | "entity.agent.<attr>" | "<variable>", "expr": "<expression>"}`. Assignments run in order, so a later one sees what an earlier one wrote. Targets and expressions both go through core/expressions.py -- a model file never executes Python.

oneOf.title: BATCH
oneOf.description: Groups parts or orders into batches, pallets or lots of a set size, or after a maximum wait, and sends the batch on as one entity. Groups entities by count: puts each arrival in the block's store and, as soon as `batch_size` items are waiting, takes exactly that many atomically to form one batch entity. Members leave live_entities and carry `in_batch` until a SEPARATE splits the batch again. With `max_wait` set, a PARTIAL batch leaves too: the timer is armed by the arrival that starts a new group and releases whatever is waiting once the oldest member has waited that long. TIE RULE: a batch that fills in the same instant as the timer expires wins and the timer releases nothing -- the same zero-delay re-check reneging uses, so the outcome never depends on the order SimPy happened to schedule two events at one timestamp. With `carrier_type` set, an arrival of that type is a CARRIER (a truck): it is not stored, and loads the stored arrivals one at a time, `member_time` each, until it holds `carrier_capacity` (default `batch_size`) or its `max_wait`, counted from its own arrival, has passed; then it leaves as itself, its members aboard. With a `pattern` too, the carrier is a pallet: each member takes the next slot of that pallet pattern, and the pallet closes when its slots are full or the next member would pass its weight limit (that member waits for the next pallet). The members carry `slot` and `layer`; the pallet carries `items`, `layers`, `load_weight`, `load_height` and `pattern`.

anyOf.description: Points where a part may leave the belt sideways: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "condition": <expression, read once as the part reaches it>, "time"?: <push time, number or expression>, "when_full"?: "wait" (default: the part waits there for room) or "pass" (it rides on), "intercept"?: true (a robot on link k + 1 picks the part on the move; its first move targets this divert), "on_late"?: what the part does when that robot is busy: "wait" (default: it stands where the robot meets it), "pass" (it rides on) or an expression, true meaning wait}. Divert k leaves by outgoing link k + 1; link 0 is the belt's end. A link may name its exit instead: source_port "out" (the end) or "d<k>", each exit once. "side"?: "left" (default) or "right" of a part travelling along the belt as seen on screen, where the divert's exit port faces on the floor plan; "angle"?: degrees from the belt's travel to that exit, above 0 and below 180 (90, the default, is square; 45 leans downstream), floor geometry only. "rule"?: a routing rule in place of the condition, {"kind", "exits"?, "conditions"?, "limit"?, "attribute"?} as a Rule-mode DECIDE's, read once as the part reaches it; "rule_group"?: a name the diverts sharing one rule all give, the rule on the first of them along the belt only; the exits are the group's diverts in belt order (names default to their ports), and an exit named "out" passes them all to the belt's end. A part counts under way until it reaches its exit's target piece or leaves a belt on its way there by a divert; name an exit "L1:L1" to stop the count at branch L1. While every exit is at its limit the part waits at the group's first divert and the belt behind packs as at a stop. Empty: none.

"side"?: "left" (default) or "right" of a part travelling along the belt as seen on screen, where the divert's exit port faces on the floor plan; "angle"?: degrees from the belt's travel to that exit, above 0 and below 180 (90, the default, is square; 45 leans downstream), floor geometry only. "rule"?: a routing rule in place of the condition, {"kind", "exits"?, "conditions"?, "limit"?, "attribute"?} as a Rule-mode DECIDE's, read once as the part reaches it; "rule_group"?: a name the diverts sharing one rule all give, the rule on the first of them along the belt only; the exits are the group's diverts in belt order (names default to their ports), and an exit named "out" passes them all to the belt's end. A part counts under way until it reaches its exit's target piece or leaves a belt on its way there by a divert; name an exit "L1:L1" to stop the count at branch L1. While every exit is at its limit the part waits at the group's first divert and the belt behind packs as at a stop. Empty: none.

anyOf.description: Points where parts from another block join the belt: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "from": <the block linking to this belt whose parts join there>, "priority"?: "belt" (default: they wait for a gap of two spacings) or "merge" (parts on the belt make room)}. anyOf.description: Photo-eyes, points that fire as a part passes: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "edge"?: "front" (default: as the part's front reaches `at`) or "back" (as its back clears `at`, a `part_length` later), "assign"?: <rows {"target", "expr"} run on that part as ASSIGN runs them>, "signal"?: <signal raised, for HOLD blocks and item code>}. Each firing is counted and traced; a queue that stands short of an eye delays it. Empty: none.

eyes.description: Photo-eyes, points that fire as a part passes: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "edge"?: "front" (default: as the part's front reaches `at`) or "back" (as its back clears `at`, a `part_length` later), "assign"?: <rows {"target", "expr"} run on that part as ASSIGN runs them>, "signal"?: <signal raised, for HOLD blocks and item code>}. Each firing is counted and traced; a queue that stands short of an eye delays it. Empty: none.

Their total is the belt's length, so set `length` to 0 and give no nodes. Empty: a straight belt of `length`.

path.description: The belt as pieces laid end to end from its entry: {"straight": <length>} or {"arc": {"radius": <r>, "angle": <degrees, up to 360>, "turn": "left" or "right" as seen on screen}}, lengths in the unit of `length`. Their total is the belt's length, so set `length` to 0 and give no nodes. Empty: a straight belt of `length`.

anyOf.description: Conveyor type: "belt", "roller", "chain", "pallet" or "mdr". Empty: an untyped belt with `spacing`, one item per cell. A typed belt has cells of `cell` and an item takes ceil((its length + `gap`) / cell) of them; `spacing` is ignored and the results' Capacity counts cells.

type.description: Conveyor type: "belt", "roller", "chain", "pallet" or "mdr". Empty: an untyped belt with `spacing`, one item per cell. A typed belt has cells of `cell` and an item takes ceil((its length + `gap`) / cell) of them; `spacing` is ignored and the results' Capacity counts cells.

gap.description: Free belt length kept between two items on a typed belt.

cell.description: Length of one cell of a typed belt; an item takes as many as its length plus `gap` needs. 0: 1 cm in any length unit. Ignored on an untyped belt.

release_delay.description: A zone's restart delay per zone from the exit, in `time_unit`.

time_unit.description: Unit of `release_delay`: "base" (the model's) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days.

anyOf.description: Accumulation zones: {"count": <zones of equal length, zone 1 at the exit>, "release_delay"?: <time, in the model's time unit unless "time_unit" says another>}. Parts accumulate as without zones; when the held exit frees, a standing part restarts release_delay times its front's zone later, never nearer than its own length to the part ahead; the end part keeps the exit unit through its delay, and a part handed to a next belt waits it before that belt takes it. Delay 0 is a belt without zones and releases the queue as one slug, as Emulate3D does at 0; Emulate3D's staggered headways at a 1 s delay (1.26 s and 0.96 s measured) differ, an open comparison. Accumulating belts with no stop or merge only. Empty: none.

zones.description: Accumulation zones: {"count": <zones of equal length, zone 1 at the exit>, "release_delay"?: <time, in the model's time unit unless "time_unit" says another>}. Parts accumulate as without zones; when the held exit frees, a standing part restarts release_delay times its front's zone later, never nearer than its own length to the part ahead; the end part keeps the exit unit through its delay, and a part handed to a next belt waits it before that belt takes it. Delay 0 is a belt without zones and releases the queue as one slug, as Emulate3D does at 0; Emulate3D's staggered headways at a 1 s delay (1.26 s and 0.96 s measured) differ, an open comparison. Accumulating belts with no stop or merge only. Empty: none.

gap.description: Free length from the last part's tail to the next part's front, in the unit of the belt's `length`.

interval.description: Front-to-front distance, never less than the last part's length on the belt, in the unit of the belt's `length`.

gap.description: Free length from the last part's tail to the next part's front, in the unit of the belt's `length`.

count.description: Parts queued before the end lets them go.

timeout.description: Longest hold since the first part stood at the end, in `time_unit`.

time_unit.description: Unit of `timeout`: "base" (the model's) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days.

anyOf.description: How parts leave the end, one form: {"metering": {"gap": <length>}} (a part leaves once the one before is that far past the end, measured from its tail), {"metering": {"interval": <length>}} (front to front, never nearer than the part before takes on the belt), {"singulation": {"gap": <length>}} (the same as metering by gap) or {"slug": {"count": <parts>, "timeout": <time>, "time_unit"?}} (the end holds until count parts are queued or timeout has passed since the first stood there, then lets them go nose to tail). Lengths are in the unit of `length` and travelled at the belt speed; the timeout is in the model's time unit unless time_unit says another. Held parts make the ones behind accumulate. A slug counts every part standing in the queue, behind a photo-eye or a stop too; a part whose place in the queue is behind a stop dwells there after the release. Each part's hold at the end is kept (in a slug the lead's; the parts let go with it hold 0). Accumulating belts without zones only. Empty: parts leave as soon as they can.

release.description: How parts leave the end, one form: {"metering": {"gap": <length>}} (a part leaves once the one before is that far past the end, measured from its tail), {"metering": {"interval": <length>}} (front to front, never nearer than the part before takes on the belt), {"singulation": {"gap": <length>}} (the same as metering by gap) or {"slug": {"count": <parts>, "timeout": <time>, "time_unit"?}} (the end holds until count parts are queued or timeout has passed since the first stood there, then lets them go nose to tail). Lengths are in the unit of `length` and travelled at the belt speed; the timeout is in the model's time unit unless time_unit says another. Held parts make the ones behind accumulate. A slug counts every part standing in the queue, behind a photo-eye or a stop too; a part whose place in the queue is behind a stop dwells there after the release. Each part's hold at the end is kept (in a slug the lead's; the parts let go with it hold 0). Accumulating belts without zones only. Empty: parts leave as soon as they can.

anyOf.description: True: the belt can run backward during a run, turned by `reverse_signal` or by item code (item.reverse). Each part on it then rides back the distance it has travelled and leaves at the start by `reverse_to`; nothing gets on until it runs forward again. Reversible belts linked end to start, with nothing between them, are one chain that turns as one: a part crosses each joint the way the chain runs. A reversible belt has no stops, diverts, merges, photo-eyes, zones or release rule.

reversible.description: True: the belt can run backward during a run, turned by `reverse_signal` or by item code (item.reverse). Each part on it then rides back the distance it has travelled and leaves at the start by `reverse_to`; nothing gets on until it runs forward again. Reversible belts linked end to start, with nothing between them, are one chain that turns as one: a part crosses each joint the way the chain runs. A reversible belt has no stops, diverts, merges, photo-eyes, zones or release rule.

anyOf.description: Signal that turns a reversible belt each time it is raised (forward, backward, forward...), with its whole chain. Empty: only item code turns it.

reverse_signal.description: Signal that turns a reversible belt each time it is raised (forward, backward, forward...), with its whole chain. Empty: only item code turns it.

anyOf.description: Exit of a reversible belt for parts leaving at its start: the target block of one of its links, or "in" (the link whose source_port is "in"); not a conveyor feeding this belt, since nothing boards a belt by its end. In a chain, only the first piece names it: a later piece hands back to the one before.

reverse_to.description: Exit of a reversible belt for parts leaving at its start: the target block of one of its links, or "in" (the link whose source_port is "in"); not a conveyor feeding this belt, since nothing boards a belt by its end. In a chain, only the first piece names it: a later piece hands back to the one before.

anyOf.description: True: the piece carries one load at a time, as a short divert or merge piece does. A load boards, at the start or at a merge, only once the piece is clear, which is when the load ahead has left, by the end or by a divert, and its tail is past the piece's end: its leave time plus (the length, less the place it left by, plus its occupied length) over the speed. Loads waiting at the start and at merges take turns in belt order; a merge with priority "merge" boards first only at the very first boarding (with several, the first by at). Not with zones, reversible, a divert with intercept or a release slug of count above 1.

one_load.description: True: the piece carries one load at a time, as a short divert or merge piece does. A load boards, at the start or at a merge, only once the piece is clear, which is when the load ahead has left, by the end or by a divert, and its tail is past the piece's end: its leave time plus (the length, less the place it left by, plus its occupied length) over the speed. Loads waiting at the start and at merges take turns in belt order; a merge with priority "merge" boards first only at the very first boarding (with several, the first by at). Not with zones, reversible, a divert with intercept or a release slug of count above 1.

anyOf.description: Length of one part along the belt, which a back-edge eye reads. 0: the spacing, or a typed belt's type zone length. On an untyped belt it is no longer than the spacing.

part_length.description: Length of one part along the belt, which a back-edge eye reads. 0: the spacing, or a typed belt's type zone length. On an untyped belt it is no longer than the spacing.

anyOf.description: Unit of `part_length`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units.

part_length_unit.description: Unit of `part_length`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units.

anyOf.description: True: the belt writes its state as model variables, read with VAR("<belt>.running") in a HOLD condition or item code: `running` (0 only while a non-accumulating belt stands for a part held at the exit it runs to), `forward` on a reversible belt (0 while it runs backward), `eye<k>.count` (eye k's firings so far) and `eye<k>.blocked` (1 while a part's body lies across eye k, front edge to back edge; not on a belt with both zones and diverts).

expose.description: True: the belt writes its state as model variables, read with VAR("<belt>.running") in a HOLD condition or item code: `running` (0 only while a non-accumulating belt stands for a part held at the exit it runs to), `forward` on a reversible belt (0 while it runs backward), `eye<k>.count` (eye k's firings so far) and `eye<k>.blocked` (1 while a part's body lies across eye k, front edge to back edge; not on a belt with both zones and diverts).

roller_diameter.description: Metres, from 0.02 to 0.3, for roller, mdr, pallet.

oneOf.title: DECIDE
oneOf.description: Routing decision: sends each part, order or customer down one of several links by percentage chance, by a condition (rework, type, size) or by a policy. "Chance" mode draws on the block's own RNG against `probs`, one probability per branch (not cumulative); "Condition" mode evaluates each of `conditions` in order and takes the first true one. Both modes take the last outgoing link as an ELSE branch when there is one more link than probs/conditions; otherwise an uncovered draw or condition fails loud rather than silently dropping the entity. "Policy" mode hands the choice to `ctx.controllers[policy]`: the number of actions is simply the number of outgoing links. A plain (synchronous) controller is called inline, in zero simulated time, exactly like Chance/Condition above. A `PausingController` (used by `nagasim.rl. SimEnv` to drive the policy from outside the run) is different: this block yields on a simpy event instead, so the whole simulation genuinely pauses until something resolves it. With no controller attached for `policy`, the block falls back to `fallback` ("first" / "random" / "shortest") so a Policy-mode model still runs and validates headless. "Rule" mode asks a routing rule (`rule`, core/routing.py) whose exits are the outgoing links; while every exit is at its limit the entity waits here, first come first served, and the rule runs again when an exit's count drops.
